newsitem.title: UK: Oil heads lower with unsold barrels plentiful.
newsitem.headline: Oil heads lower with unsold barrels plentiful.

text.p: Oil prices eased on Monday as a sickly outlook for the key Atlantic Basin physical crude market overcame early speculative buying.
London futures for benchmark May Brent closed 24 cents down at $19.52 a barrel after reaching a three-week high on Friday.

Dealers said buying interest from the investment funds which closely track commodity price trends supported a modest early rally, but the failure to breach key technical resistance levels pushed the market down again.
"I see very little to get excited about on the buy side. I think (traders) saw it as a good selling opportunity," said one futures broker in London.
Meanwhile, physical traders took a pessimistic view of the balance for supply and demand as spot market cargoes sold on Monday at growing discounts to the futures market.
Brent slipped to $18.68 a barrel two weeks ago from just below $25 in mid-January.
Traders in the United States were looking for fresh signs of a revival for gasoline, which traditionally lends support to the oil complex in spring.
U.S. gasoline inventories are at a significant deficit to year-ago levels as the industry gears up for the spring and summer driving seasons.
Refinery profit margins in Europe and the United States recovered a little last week from recent lows but still remain at depressed levels.
But margins in Singapore, Asia's benchmark refining centre, soared to average $5.40 a barrel on a barrel of Middle East Dubai crude.
That has helped spark renewed buying interest from Asian refiners for West African crudes. China took a large cargo on Monday. NYMEX light crude futures (Apr) $20.92 $21.29
